subject: science
promptStrong: Give me a challenging KS3 exam-style question on {lo}, then mark my answer.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for KS3 simply, with a worked example and the most common mistake.
learningObjectives: Chromosomes, genes and DNA and how they fit together

questions.lo: Chromosomes, genes and DNA and how they fit together
questions.q: In a human cell, where is DNA found?
options: Floating loose in the cytoplasm
Inside the nucleus, packaged into chromosomes
Only on the cell membrane
Only in red blood cells
questions.explain: DNA is coiled up into chromosomes and stored inside the cell's nucleus. It is not loose in the cytoplasm, and it is found in nearly all body cells (red blood cells are an exception because they lose their nucleus).

questions.lo: Chromosomes, genes and DNA and how they fit together
questions.q: Which of these correctly describes how the structures fit together?
options: A chromosome is a section of a gene
A gene is a section of DNA, and DNA is coiled up to form a chromosome
DNA is a section of a gene
A gene contains many chromosomes
questions.explain: A chromosome is made of a long coiled DNA molecule, and a gene is just a short section of that DNA carrying the information for one feature. So the order from largest to smallest is chromosome, then gene, then DNA base.

questions.lo: Genes carry the information for features
questions.q: What is a gene?
options: A section of DNA that carries the instructions for a feature
A type of cell found only in the brain
The jelly that fills a cell
The membrane around the nucleus
questions.explain: A gene is a section of DNA that codes for a particular feature, such as eye colour. Different genes carry different sets of instructions.

questions.lo: Chromosomes, genes and DNA and how they fit together
questions.q: How many chromosomes are found in a normal human body cell?
questions.explain: Human body cells contain 46 chromosomes, arranged as 23 pairs. You inherit one chromosome of each pair from each parent.

questions.lo: Heredity: passing genetic information from parents to offspring
questions.q: What does the term 'heredity' mean?
options: The way animals learn skills from their parents
The passing of genetic information from parents to offspring
The way the environment changes an organism
The death of a whole species
questions.explain: Heredity is the passing of genetic information (genes) from parents to offspring. It is why offspring resemble their parents, though they are not identical.

questions.lo: Heredity: passing genetic information from parents to offspring
questions.q: A child has features that look a bit like each parent. Why?
options: The child copied both parents' behaviour
The child inherited a mixture of genes, some from each parent
The child chose which features to have
The environment made the child look like the parents
questions.explain: In sexual reproduction the offspring inherits a mixture of genes from both parents, so it shows a blend of inherited features from each.

questions.lo: Variation between species and within a species
questions.q: Two Labrador dogs are different heights. This is an example of variation of which kind?
options: Variation between species
Variation within a species
No variation at all
Extinction
questions.explain: Both dogs belong to the same species, so differences between them are variation within a species. Variation between species would be, for example, a dog compared with a cat.

questions.lo: Variation between species and within a species
questions.q: Which pair shows variation BETWEEN species?
options: Two humans with different hair colours
A cat and a dog
Two roses of slightly different height
Two apples from the same tree
questions.explain: A cat and a dog are different species, so the differences between them are variation between species. The other options are all differences within a single species.

questions.lo: Genetic and environmental causes of variation
questions.q: A person has a scar from a childhood accident. What type of variation is this?
options: Genetic variation
Environmental variation
It will be inherited by their children
It is caused by their DNA
questions.explain: A scar is caused by an injury, which is part of the environment, so it is environmental variation. It is not stored in the genes and is not passed on to offspring.

questions.lo: Genetic and environmental causes of variation
questions.q: A person's height is affected by their genes and also by how well they were fed as they grew. Height is therefore caused by:
options: Genes only
The environment only
Both genes and the environment
Neither genes nor the environment
questions.explain: Many features, including height, are caused by a combination of inherited genes and environmental factors such as diet. It is a common mistake to think all variation is only genetic.

questions.lo: Genetic and environmental causes of variation
questions.q: Which feature is caused mainly by genes (genetic variation)?
options: A suntan
Natural eye colour
A language someone speaks
A broken bone
questions.explain: Natural eye colour is inherited, so it is genetic variation. A suntan, a spoken language and a broken bone are all caused by the environment.

questions.lo: Competition, adaptation and survival
questions.q: In a population of rabbits, some run faster than others. In an area with foxes, why might the faster rabbits do better?
options: They are more likely to escape foxes, survive and reproduce
They decide to run faster when they see a fox
They stop being rabbits
Speed makes no difference to survival
questions.explain: Faster rabbits are better suited (adapted) to escaping predators, so they are more likely to survive and reproduce, passing on the genes for speed. This is natural selection in action.

questions.lo: Natural selection and the work of Charles Darwin
questions.q: Which scientist is famous for the theory of evolution by natural selection?
options: Isaac Newton
Charles Darwin
Marie Curie
Charles Dickens
questions.explain: Charles Darwin proposed the theory of evolution by natural selection, published most famously in On the Origin of Species in 1859.

questions.lo: Natural selection and the work of Charles Darwin
questions.q: Which statement best describes how natural selection produces long-necked giraffes?
options: Each giraffe stretched its neck and passed the longer neck on
Giraffes wanted longer necks so their bodies grew them
By chance some giraffes had longer necks; they fed better, survived and passed the gene on
The trees forced the giraffes' necks to grow
questions.explain: Natural selection acts on variation that already exists by chance. Giraffes with longer necks reached more food, survived better and passed the gene on. Animals do not 'try' to change or stretch a feature into existence.

questions.lo: Natural selection and the work of Charles Darwin
questions.q: Put the steps of natural selection in the correct order.
options: Variation exists; competition to survive; best-suited survive and reproduce; helpful genes become more common
All individuals are identical; they all survive; nothing changes
Animals choose a new feature; they grow it; they pass it on
The environment stays the same; species never change
questions.explain: Natural selection follows this sequence: there is variation, individuals compete to survive, the best-suited survive and reproduce, and the helpful genes become more common over generations.

questions.lo: Evolution as change over many generations
questions.q: Over roughly what timescale does evolution usually happen?
options: Within a single animal's lifetime
A few weeks
Many generations, over thousands to millions of years
Instantly, when the environment changes
questions.explain: Evolution is the gradual change of a species across many generations, usually over thousands to millions of years. An individual does not evolve during its own life; the population changes over time.

questions.lo: Evolution as change over many generations
questions.q: What is the main evidence that shows how living things have changed over very long periods of time?
options: Weather records
Fossils
Photographs
Family trees
questions.explain: Fossils are the preserved remains of organisms from the past. Comparing fossils of different ages gives evidence for how species have changed, supporting the theory of evolution.

questions.lo: Environmental change, poor adaptation and extinction
questions.q: What does it mean for a species to become extinct?
options: It moves to a new habitat
Every member of the species has died out, with none left
It changes into a slightly different colour
It goes to sleep for the winter
questions.explain: Extinction means that all members of a species have died and none remain anywhere. The dinosaurs are a well-known example.

questions.lo: Environmental change, poor adaptation and extinction
questions.q: A large environmental change (such as a rapid climate change) can lead to extinction because:
options: Species always die when seasons change
Some species become less well adapted, so too few can survive and reproduce
Animals decide to stop breeding
Extinction has nothing to do with the environment
questions.explain: If the environment changes, a species may no longer be well suited to it. If too few individuals can survive and reproduce, the whole species can die out — extinction.

questions.lo: Environmental change, poor adaptation and extinction
questions.q: A beetle species is perfectly camouflaged on green leaves. The area is cleared and replaced with brown soil. What is the likely effect?
options: The beetles become easier for predators to see, so more are eaten and the species is at greater risk
The beetles instantly turn brown by choice
Nothing changes because camouflage never matters
The predators die instead
questions.explain: When the environment changes, the beetles' green camouflage no longer helps. They are easier to spot and eat, so the species becomes less well adapted and is at greater risk of decline or extinction unless brown variants already exist for selection to act on.

specSource: National Curriculum in England: science programme of study, Key Stage 3; Biology — Genetics and evolution
